newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania sues tobacco industry over Medicaid.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania sues tobacco industry over Medicaid.

text.p: Pennysylvania filed suit against the largest tobacco companies to seek to recover possibly over $1 billion in Medicaid bills the state has paid to treat people suffering from tobacco-related illnesses.
In the complaint filed by Pennsylvania Attorney General Mike Fisher, the state, among other things, charged the tobacco companies of conspiring to entice children to smoke.

Fisher said a core issue raised in the state's complaint, in which it joins other states in efforts to recover huge sums from the industry, was that tobacco companies "deliberately marketed cigarettes and other tobacco products to children, thus abetting the sale of tobacco to minors.
"This is a fight about protecting the public health and safety of young people of our Commonwealth," Fisher said.
"When Joe Camel is as familiar to six-year olds as Mickey Mouse, there's a problem."
Fisher expects Pennsylvania's claim "could exceed $1 billion."

In its complaint, the state also contends that the tobacco industry knew decades ago that smoking causes deadly diseases, including cancer, emphysema and heart disease and deliberately hid those facts.
The industry also knowingly manipulated the nicotine content of cigarettes, with the intention of hooking as many people as possible on smoking, particularly children, for as long as possible.
At the same time, the tobacco industry deliberately suppressed research on and development of a safer cigarrette, the state contends.

Named in the suit filed in the Common Pleas Court in Philadelphia are Philip Morris Inc, R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp, B.A.T. Industries P.L.C., American Tobacco Co Inc, Lorillard Tobacco Co, Liggett Group Inc, United States Tobacco Co, Tobacco Institute Inc, the Council for Tobacco Ressearch-U.S.A. Inc, Smokeless Tobacco Council Inc and public relations firm Hill and Knowlton Inc.
